trigger: tag_store pool-acquire timeout or not-open on the FIRST tag read (get_distinct_keys) while the roster and device-CI reads succeed, then an operator opens the Hardware list or GET /api/v1/hardware
classification_rationale: docs/user-manual/inventory.md promises a "Tags unavailable" banner on a whole-store tag degrade, but a failed get_distinct_keys() is value_or({})-ed to an empty key list and TagStore::get_values_for_keys({}) returns success on empty keys BEFORE its open_ check (tag_store.cpp:611-612), so tags_degraded stays false. Verified by the orchestrator reading both sites; the same line exists on origin/dev (server.cpp:17747).
summary: build_hw_roster (a function this PR edits) masks a failed tag-key read as "no tags": blank Tags column, tag= filter returns an authoritative-looking empty table, REST tags_degraded:false. In-grain fix (~3 lines, no new seam surface): if get_distinct_keys() fails set result.tags_degraded = true. Alex ruling needed if deferred instead (precedent 2026-10-06 defer+issue for run C's pre-existing HIGH). Issue draft 01.

trigger: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE (or a long lock) on endpoint_state.endpoints with default pool GUCs (lock_timeout 10 s, statement_timeout 30 s) while operators and clients keep issuing list/REST/viz/MCP roster reads
classification_rationale: Only the pool ACQUIRE is bounded (2 s, 500 ms saturated); the SELECT then holds a lease and an httplib worker for up to lock_timeout/statement_timeout. The banner text "Retry shortly" and 400 ms keyup search re-fire it; the 16-lease pool can fill and starve audit/auth/rbac acquires. Wait is bounded, so not an I5 HIGH case; the same wait existed before and was silent, now user-visible. This change did not add the wait.
summary: Roster read can pin a pool lease for the PG statement/lock timeout during a table-lock incident, amplified by retries. File as a reliability follow-up (issue draft 03); do not fix here (#4441 point-read and pool-level timeouts are separate work).

trigger: roster outage plus any admitted Inventory:Read holder requesting GET /api/v1/hardware/<id> with an id that does not exist and is long or carries CR/LF/C0 bytes
classification_rationale: The new REST 503 arm audits the raw caller-supplied agent_id as target_id for an id that previously 404ed unaudited. No length/C0 floor (viz host route and MCP twin have one: kMaxAgentIdLength + C0 reject, B3 Gate 8). Pre-existing sibling sites: /fragments/hardware/ci (:286-289) and the REST success arm audit raw ids too, so zero marginal capability. DERIVATION CONTESTED: security-guardian, compliance-officer and unhappy-path derive LOW (I8: the row is persisted faithfully, AuditStore scrubs UTF-8/NUL, no in-repo flattening consumer exists: I grepped for syslog/forwarders and found none); consistency-auditor CON-2 derives I1 (CWE-117) -> HIGH by the viz precedent, with the harm path (an external consumer that flattens rows) unnamed. Escalates to HIGH if the orchestrator rules I1 applies.
summary: Recommended fold regardless of band (~12 lines, mirrors viz_routes.cpp:359-371): 400 for size() > auth::kMaxAgentIdLength or any byte < 0x20 at the top of the REST record route and the CI fragment. Issue draft 04 if not folded.
